rules.statement: Store only a hash (such as SHA-256) of a bearer secret like a setup or bootstrap token, compare a presented value against it with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, and never log the configured secret.
rules.why: A configured token must stay unrecoverable from server state or logs, and a constant-time comparison stops timing attacks on the token check.
rules.check: Look for plaintext token fields kept in memory or persisted, comparisons that use `==`, `string.Equals` or `SequenceEqual`, and log statements that include the token value.

rules.statement: Keep any state that decides whether a one-time or cross-replica operation is allowed in the shared database, not in process memory or the local file system.
rules.why: Replicas share only the database, so state held in memory or on local disk lets replicas disagree and an operation run more than once.
rules.check: Look for static fields, singletons, in-memory caches or local files that gate an operation such as setup or initialization in a multi-replica host.

rules.statement: Make a single-use operation mark itself used in the same save as its effect, and guard that save with an optimistic concurrency token so a concurrent second attempt fails.
rules.why: If the 'used' mark goes in a separate save, a crash or a race can let the operation run twice, for example creating two root administrators.
rules.check: Look for a one-time action whose completion flag is written in a separate SaveChanges call or transaction, or whose row has no concurrency token checked on update.

rules.statement: Stage every entity in a multi-part provisioning operation on one unit of work and save it once, so that a failed validation of any part saves nothing.
rules.why: A refused part, such as a client registration, must not leave the other parts, such as a root administrator, saved without it.
rules.check: Look for provisioning code that calls save between creating related entities, or that keeps earlier saves after a later validation fails.

rules.statement: Build absolute links and addresses returned to clients from configured or stored values, such as the tenant's issuer, never from the request's Host header or the browser's location.
rules.why: Request-derived host values can be spoofed, and addresses must reflect the configured identity of the instance.
rules.check: Look for `HttpRequest.Host`, `Request.Scheme` or a client-supplied URL used to build links in responses where a configured issuer or base URL exists.

rules.statement: When an endpoint answers 429 Too Many Requests, include a `Retry-After` header with the seconds until the next allowed attempt and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
rules.why: Clients need to know when to retry, and rate-limit responses on sensitive endpoints must not be cached.
rules.check: Look for rate-limiter rejection handlers or 429 results that omit `Retry-After` or `Cache-Control: no-store`.

rules.statement: In browser code, pass a secret in a link through the URL fragment, never the query string, and remove it from the address bar with `history.replaceState` once it has been read.
rules.why: A fragment never reaches the server or a Referer header, and stripping it keeps the secret out of history and screenshots.
rules.check: Look for tokens read from `location.search` or sent as query parameters, and for fragment secrets that are read and then left in the URL.

rules.statement: Import a client's JWK Set by value only after a public-key parser refuses any key with private members.
rules.why: A client's key set must hold only public keys, and private key material must never be accepted or stored.
rules.check: Look for JWK Set import or parsing paths that accept keys without checking for private parameters (such as `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi` or `k`).

rules.statement: Return deployment-layout details, such as other services' URLs and client IDs, only from an endpoint that checks the caller's credential, never from an anonymous status endpoint.
rules.why: An anonymous endpoint would show the deployment's layout to anyone, so only a holder of the token may learn it.
rules.check: Look for anonymous or unauthenticated endpoints whose response includes internal URLs, client IDs or other deployment topology.

rules.statement: Add only the specific origins a page needs to a page's Content-Security-Policy `connect-src`, never a wildcard or an origin taken from user input or the URL.
rules.why: A link that someone else wrote could otherwise make the page read data, such as keys, from an origin that the deployment does not name.
rules.check: Look for `connect-src` values built with `*`, `https:` or origins taken from request parameters, fragments or form input.
